clue.text: Philadelphia, for example, backing Congress leader's role

indicators.note: one piece backs or supports the other, standing after it
the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Congress is used

parts.note: Philadelphia is a city in Pennsylvania, abbreviated PA: a PA city

explanation.surface: A Philadelphia figure is supporting the role of the man at the head of Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Philadelphia, for example' as 'a PA city' (PA = Pennsylvania), and put the C from 'Congress leader' in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A capacity is a role or position, as in acting in an advisory capacity.

clue.text: Butterfly or bluebottle

definitions.meaning: bluebottle is old slang for a policeman

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a copper butterfly, and copper as slang for a police officer.

clue.text: Test cricketer getting single is caught by expert bowling

indicators.note: one piece is caught, held inside the other

parts.note: a pro is an expert
a bowler who is bowling is said to be on
a bat is a batsman in cricket
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A Test cricketer scores a single but is caught off a skilled bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides the definition: 'Test' is a trial period. A bowler who is bowling is 'on' in cricket talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Probation is a trial period in which someone is tested before being confirmed.

clue.text: City accommodating holy man in comfort

indicators.note: the holy man is placed in the word for comfort

parts.note: to cheer is to comfort
ST is short for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A city takes in a holy man and makes him comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is a cathedral city in north-west England.

clue.text: To highly trained soldiers, are they the "dogs of war'"?

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service

explanation.surface: A question whether elite troops are the famous dogs of war.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'dogs of war' are not mercenaries here but real dogs: the tosa is a Japanese fighting breed. SAS is Britain's elite regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosas are Japanese mastiffs bred for dog fighting, hence literal dogs of war.

clue.text: I pinch change to add to the kitty

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of I pinch

explanation.surface: Someone confessing to a little theft from the shared fund.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is an idiom for contributing money to a shared fund.

clue.text: Sailors' cry, given sack

definitions.meaning: a chant sung by sailors heaving on ropes
to be given the sack is to be dismissed

explanation.definitionFit: It is a shanty cry when hauling, and 'given the heave-ho' means dismissed from a job.

clue.text: Soldier turned up with cargo of petroleum

indicators.note: a cargo is carried inside, so one piece holds the other
the word up is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: petroleum is oil

explanation.surface: A soldier arrives with a load of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses 'up' to give PU, which carries OIL as cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: A poilu was a French infantryman, especially of the First World War.

clue.text: Corrupt salesmen not easily identified?

indicators.note: corrupt suggests the letters of salesmen are spoilt and jumbled

explanation.surface: Dishonest sales staff are hard to track down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without a name, or anonymous, is hard to identify.

clue.text: Entire business said to fold: millions CONE needed for investment

clue.text: Skill developed in English soaps or films

indicators.note: film is developed, and here the letters are developed into a new order

explanation.surface: Acting talent nurtured in British TV serials or cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes IN as well as E, SOAPS, OR and FILMS: fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Professionalism is the skill and competence expected of an expert.

clue.text: Rejected religious teaching as originally taught by American theologian

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: RE is religious education, taught in British schools

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of taught is used

explanation.surface: A theologian whose religious doctrine, as he first taught it in America, was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education, a British school subject) is turned back to ER by 'Rejected'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erastus was a 16th-century Swiss theologian who held that the state should rule the church.

clue.text: What happened before? Question posed during quiet part of film

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical sign for quiet

indicators.note: the question goes in during, in the middle of, the other pieces

parts.note: a reel is one part of a film

explanation.surface: A query raised in a hushed moment of a movie about earlier events.
explanation.definitionFit: A prequel is a story set before the events of an earlier work.

clue.text: Display sack for weapon

parts.note: to air something is to display it
to rifle or sack a place is to plunder it

explanation.surface: A display of a bag used as a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An air rifle is a gun that fires pellets by compressed air.

clue.text: Gunfire caused damage round one Check to statue

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Gunfire caused damage round one Check to statue': 'Check to' is OCR noise beyond a letter misread and the scan crop is blank; wordplay appears to be an anagram of GUNFIRE round I
annotationWithheld.clue: Gunfire caused damage round one Check to statue

clue.text: Conspirator delivers speech, having deposed king

indicators.note: deposing removes from power, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: orates means makes a speech
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A plotter makes a speech after overthrowing the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: R (rex, Latin for king) is removed from ORATES. Titus Oates invented the Popish Plot of 1678.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Oates fabricated the Popish Plot against Charles II, a conspirator of English history.

clue.text: The Great Escape was so good? (3,6) minute.

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'The Great Escape was so good? (3,6) minute.': trailing '(3,6) minute.' is OCR noise beyond a letter misread and the scan crop is blank; appears to be a cryptic definition
annotationWithheld.clue: The Great Escape was so good? (3,6) minute.

clue.text: One frequently gets depressed, having to keep characters apart

definitions.text: One frequently gets depressed, having to keep characters apart

parts.words: One frequently gets depressed, having to keep characters apart
parts.note: sounds like a lonely person, but describes the keyboard key pressed to separate typed letters

explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard bar is pressed often to insert gaps between typed characters.

clue.text: Party drink is a hit

definitions.meaning: a mixed drink served from a bowl at parties

explanation.definitionFit: Punch is both a fruity party drink and a blow with the fist.

clue.text: Fundamentalist group keeps one unenlightened

parts.note: to have is to keep
I is the Roman numeral one
dim means dull or unenlightened

explanation.surface: A hardline sect retains a member who is not very bright.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hasidim are a strictly orthodox Jewish movement.

clue.text: Wild animal appearing at last on a video?

indicators.note: at last tells us only the final letter of appearing is used

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a video is a tape

explanation.surface: A wild beast finally shows up on film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing at last' gives G, its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A great ape is a gorilla, chimpanzee or orangutan, a wild animal.

clue.text: With Old Bill entering, bound to have cringed

indicators.note: one piece enters, going inside the other

parts.note: tied means bound
an ad is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: With the police arriving, someone bound is cowering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' looks like British slang for the police, but splits into O (old) and AD (bill).
explanation.definitionFit: To toady is to fawn or grovel, so toadied is close to cringed.

clue.text: Hold a column for him

definitions.meaning: ... Column in London's Trafalgar Square honours the admiral

explanation.definitionFit: It is a wrestling hold and the admiral whose column stands in Trafalgar Square.

clue.text: In speech, huntsman is not so refined '

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a courser is one who hunts with hounds

explanation.surface: A hunter is less polished than others.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarser means rougher or less refined.

clue.text: A player on the field causing dread

parts.note: a wing is a player on the flank in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A footballer instils fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Awing means filling with awe, a mix of dread and wonder.

clue.text: Cocaine or dope?

definitions.meaning: British slang for a fool, a dope

explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is slang for cocaine and for a fool, the two senses of dope.

clue.text: Taxi taking queen's trunk

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A taxi carries the Queen's luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' looks like luggage, but it is a tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A caber is a tree trunk tossed in Scottish Highland games.

clue.text: Telford frequently was working towards rapprochement

definitions.meaning: Thomas Telford, the Scottish engineer, constructed many bridges

explanation.definitionFit: Telford literally constructed bridges, and figuratively it means reconciling parties.

clue.text: Overturned measure taken by current German government

indicators.note: overturned turns the whole run of pieces upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: an em is a printer's measure
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A government overturned a measure brought in by the current German regime.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a government, especially an authoritarian one.

clue.text: Loan to be paid by community in Devon

parts.note: credit is money lent
something on the slate or on account is still to be paid

explanation.surface: A loan to be repaid by a local community.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crediton is a market town in mid Devon.
